question: What is the meaning of environmental costs and benefits beyond the system boundary of the structure d in relation to sustainability, environmental cost indicators?
data_point: environmental costs and benefits beyond the system boundary of the structure d
description: Environmental costs and benefits beyond the system boundary of a structure in relation to sustainability refer to the impacts on the environment that extend beyond the direct boundaries of the building or product being assessed. These costs and benefits consider factors such as raw material extraction, transportation, manufacturing processes, operational energy and water use, maintenance, repair, end-of-life disposal, and potential reuse or recycling. Environmental cost indicators aim to evaluate the environmental impact of a structure throughout its entire life cycle, taking into account not only the direct impacts but also the broader environmental consequences associated with its production, use, and disposal.
